anf_compare.notes: An NPNF English exists under Basil, Letter 260; it was read only to confirm the text's identity and the two readings taken by sense, not for wording.

bible_refs.method: allusion: the Hebrew slave set free after six years of service, in the seventh
bible_refs.note: δι' ἑπτὰ ἐτῶν ὁ Ἑβραῖος ἀπελύετο τῆς δουλείας.

bible_refs.method: allusion: seven weeks of years make the Jubilee, with release proclaimed
bible_refs.note: The Jubilee; the letter adds the land's sabbath, the cancelling of debts and release from slavery.

choices.why: Continues 'the Lord did not move on to another number, but…': the number seven is what is multiplied.
διά with the genitive of time: at the end of seven years (Exodus 21:2).
ὀνομαστός is renowned; the subject is the seven weeks of years (Leviticus 25:8-10).

choices.term: ὃς διὰ τῶν ἑπτὰ ἡμερῶν ἀνακυκλούμενος ἡμᾶς παρατρέχει
choices.english: which circles round through the seven days and runs past us
choices.why: The age turns through the week and passes us by.
rejected: which runs us through by means of the seven days

choices.why: ἔκτισις is payment of a penalty: lesser sins are paid for in this age so that we escape endless punishment.

pass_a_gloss: [continuing 'but the'] seven, having multiplied [it], in it he set the limit. And after seven years the Hebrew was let go from slavery. And seven weeks of years were making the famous Jubilee for those of long ago, in which the earth kept sabbath, and there were cuttings-off of debts, and a release from slavery; and as it were a new life was being set up from the start in the number of seven, the old one in a certain manner receiving its end. And these [are] types of this age, which, circling back through the seven days, runs past us; in which the payments of the more moderate sins come about, according to the man-loving care of the good Master, so that we are not handed over to punishment in the age without end. The 'seven times', then, [is] because of the kinship toward this world, as of the men who love the world, from them…
pass_b_english: …multiplied the seven and set the limit within it. And after seven years the Hebrew was set free from slavery (Exodus 21:2). Seven weeks of years made up the renowned Jubilee for the people of old (Leviticus 25:8–10), in which the land kept sabbath, debts were cancelled, and there was release from slavery; and in the number seven a new life, as it were, began afresh, with the old in a way reaching its completion.

These things are types of this present age, which circles round through the seven days and runs past us. In it the penalties for lesser sins are paid off, in keeping with the loving care of the good Master, so that we may not be handed over to punishment in the endless age. The “seven times,” then, is used because of its kinship with this world, as with world-loving people, from them…
source_text:
ἑπτὰ πολυπλασιάσας, ἐν αὐτῷ τὸν ὅρον ἔθετο. Καὶ δι' ἑπτὰ ἐτῶν ὁ Ἑβραῖος ἀπελύετο
τῆς δουλείας. Ἑπτὰ δὲ ἑβδομάδες ἐτῶν τὸ ὀνομαστὸν Ἰωβίλαιον ἐποίουν τοῖς πάλαι,
ἐν ᾧ ἐσαββάτιζεν ἡ γῆ, χρεῶν δὲ ἦσαν ἀποκοπαὶ, καὶ δουλείας ἀπαλλαγὴ, καὶ οἱονεὶ
νέος ἄνωθεν καθίστατο βίος ἐν τῷ ἑβδοματικῷ ἀριθμῷ, τοῦ παλαιοῦ τρόπον τινὰ
τὴν συντέλειαν δεχομένου.
Ταῦτα δὲ τύποι τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου, ὃς διὰ τῶν ἑπτὰ ἡμερῶν
ἀνακυκλούμενος ἡμᾶς παρατρέχει· ἐν ᾧ γίνονται αἱ τῶν μετριωτέρων ἁμαρτημάτων
ἐκτίσεις, κατὰ τὴν φιλάνθρωπον ἐπιμέλειαν τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ ∆εσπότου, ὡς μὴ τῷ
ἀπεράντῳ αἰῶνι παραδοθῆναι ἡμᾶς εἰς κόλασιν. Τὸ μὲν οὖν ἑπτάκις, διὰ τὴν πρὸς
τὸν κόσμον τοῦτον συγγένειαν ὡς τῶν φιλοκόσμων ἀνθρώπων ἀπ' αὐτῶν
reviewer: claude (Wave A review, clause by clause against the Greek)
review_notes: Author: this letter is Basil of Caesarea's Letter 260, to Bishop Optimus. PG 77 prints it among the letters of Cyril of Alexandria as Letter 80.

Retranslated from the rv0 review: 'multiplied the seven', 'after seven years' (Exodus 21:2), 'renowned' for ὀνομαστόν, Leviticus 25:8-10 for the Jubilee, 'circles round … and runs past us', 'penalties … paid off' for ἐκτίσεις, 'world-loving' for φιλοκόσμων.
The copy-text writes the D of Δεσπότου with the sign ∆ (U+2206); read as Δεσπότου, 'Master'. The copy-text breaks off mid-sentence after ἀπ' αὐτῶν.
